outcome.technical: Written by the orchestrator (guard command-reading code). guard-secrets-read: new `_shell_word_at` reads a redirect target as the whole shell word (quotes and escapes removed, ending at an unquoted unescaped blank/operator or a group closer) when the target starts outside quotes - `> 'src/a b.py'` was read as `src/a` and the write went ungraded; inside a quoted string another program runs the bare token is kept as before; `tee` operands are split by `_config.shell_words` on the same condition. Refusals are signed by the rule: `PLAN_GATE_TAG` heads the plan-gate templates (_PLAN_WRITE_DENY/ASK, _BEYOND_DENY/ASK) and `_signed` adds `[guard-secrets-read]` only to a message that names no rule. _config.program_candidates returns the floor candidates an exact outer wrapper collected beside an uncertain inner one's fallback. _config.effective_cwd returns no answer for a doubled backslash (escaped backslash + word break) and an escaped leading dash. A bracket stays a literal path character (route directories like `[locale]`), documented in SECURITY.md rather than added to UNRESOLVED_MARKS, which would stop grading those writes. The heredoc-after-cd write (installed 3.2.0 refused a declared file after `cd`) is pinned as cdh1/cdh2 and passes on this tree: fixed before 3.3.0, now held.
